papers.title: Microstructures and unique low thermal expansion of Invar 36 alloy fabricated by selective laser melting

corresponding_authors.name: Kai Wei
corresponding_authors.affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Advanced Design and Manufacturing for Vehicle Body, Hunan University, Changsha, Hunan 410082, PR China

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究Invar 36合金的微结构和低热膨胀性能，与生物医学植入物设计和力学无关。
llm.why_not_core: No biomedical context, no stress shielding or stiffness matching, no fatigue or osseointegration.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究选区激光熔融制备Invar 36合金的微观结构及其独特低热膨胀性能。
summary_zh.method: 采用SLM工艺制备样品，并通过微观表征和热膨胀测试分析性能。
summary_zh.result: 成功获得低热膨胀系数合金，微观结构均匀。
summary_zh.validation: 通过XRD、SEM和热膨胀仪进行实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the microstructures and low thermal expansion behavior of Invar 36 alloy fabricated by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Samples were fabricated by SLM and characterized using XRD, SEM, and dilatometry.
summary_en.result: The SLM-fabricated Invar 36 exhibited a unique low coefficient of thermal expansion with uniform microstructure.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through microstructural analysis and thermal expansion measurements.

papers.title: Microstructure evolution and cracking behaviors of additively manufactured AlxCrCuFeNi2 high entropy alloys via selective laser melting

corresponding_authors.name: Zemin Wang
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Wuhan National Laboratory for Optoelectronics, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, 430074, PR China

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究高熵合金的微观组织与开裂行为，不涉及生物医用植入物设计或应力遮挡等关键问题。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address biomedical implant design, porous structures, stress shielding, fatigue behavior, or osseointegration; it focuses on high entropy alloys processing and cracking.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究SLM制备高熵合金的微观组织与开裂行为。
summary_zh.method: 通过改变Al含量制备AlxCrCuFeNi2合金，分析其微观结构。
summary_zh.result: 揭示了成分对微观组织和裂纹敏感性的影响。

summary_en.motivation: This study investigates the microstructure evolution and cracking mechanisms of additively manufactured AlxCrCuFeNi2 high entropy alloys via selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: A series of alloys with varying Al content were fabricated by SLM and characterized using SEM, EBSD, and XRD.
summary_en.result: The results show that increasing Al content leads to a transition from FCC to BCC phases and influences cracking susceptibility.
summary_en.validation: Microstructural observations and phase analysis were used to validate the findings.

papers.title: Advances in the Research of Bioinks Based on Natural Collagen, Polysaccharide and Their Derivatives for Skin 3D Bioprinting.
papers.abstract: The skin plays an important role in protecting the human body, and wound healing must be set in motion immediately following injury or trauma to restore the normal structure and function of skin. The extracellular matrix component of the skin mainly consists of collagen, glycosaminoglycan (GAG), elastin and hyaluronic acid (HA). Recently, natural collagen, polysaccharide and their derivatives such as collagen, gelatin, alginate, chitosan and pectin have been selected as the matrix materials of bioink to construct a functional artificial skin due to their biocompatible and biodegradable properties by 3D bioprinting, which is a revolutionary technology with the potential to transform both research and medical therapeutics. In this review, we outline the current skin bioprinting technologies and the bioink components for skin bioprinting. We also summarize the bioink products practiced in research recently and current challenges to guide future research to develop in a promising direction. While there are challenges regarding currently available skin bioprinting, addressing these issues will facilitate the rapid advancement of 3D skin bioprinting and its ability to mimic the native anatomy and physiology of skin and surrounding tissues in the future.

summary_zh.method: 总结了胶原、多糖及其衍生物作为生物墨水的现状。

summary_zh.validation: 无实验验证，为文献综述。

summary_en.motivation: This review summarizes the current state of natural collagen, polysaccharide, and their derivatives as bioink materials for skin 3D bioprinting.
summary_en.method: The paper surveys existing skin bioprinting technologies and bioink components, focusing on biocompatible and biodegradable natural polymers.
summary_en.result: It identifies key challenges such as mimicking native skin anatomy and physiology, and outlines future research directions.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation is performed; this is a literature review.
